name: bird-03-coupling-interval
question:
Can the reactor coupling/update interval be exposed as a tunable parameter,
and does the coupled trajectory converge as the interval decreases?
hypothesis:
Making the interval configurable and shrinking it produces a convergent
dissolved-O2 trajectory (changes below tolerance under interval halving),
so the interval can trade fidelity against cost without changing the
qualitative result.
objective:
Expose the coupling interval as a parameter and measure the dissolved-O2
trajectory across interval values to determine convergence behavior.
description:
The BiRD coupling interval is currently fixed. This study parameterizes it
and characterizes convergence, resolving the coupler-timestep-tunability
question raised by v2ecoli mbp-03. Builds on the live coupled loop from
bird-02.

expected_behavior.name: coupling-interval-is-configurable
expected_behavior.en: The coupling/update interval is a process parameter with a documented default, and runs honor the configured value.
expected_behavior.notes: Verified by tests/test_bird03_coupling_interval.py::test_coupling_interval_is_configurable — the interval is a composite parameter threaded onto both processes; runs honor it (smaller interval → more steps for the same horizon).

expected_behavior.name: coupled-trajectory-converges-as-interval-decreases
expected_behavior.en: Halving the coupling interval changes the dissolved-O2 trajectory by less than a stated tolerance — convergence rather than interval-dependence.
expected_behavior.notes: Verified by tests/test_bird03_coupling_interval.py::test_coupled_trajectory_converges_as_interval_decreases — DO at a fixed time converges to a fine reference as the interval halves (errors strictly decreasing; finest < 0.005 mg/L). Cross-run convergence isn't expressible in the dashboard grammar (issue #96), hence pytest.
